ux_guidelines.description: WCAG 2.2 AA says authentication must not depend only on a cognitive function test unless an exception applies

ux_guidelines.dont: Block paste or require manual OTP transcription with no alternative

ux_guidelines.description: Auto-rotating content needs user control
ux_guidelines.do: Provide previous next and play/pause; stop on focus or hover and when reduced motion is requested
ux_guidelines.dont: Auto-advance slides without a stop control

ux_guidelines.description: An error summary for failed validation complements inline field errors and must be easy to find by keyboard and screen reader users
ux_guidelines.do: Place it at the top of the form; move focus to its heading or container after failed submit; link each item to its invalid field; retain inline errors
ux_guidelines.dont: Replace inline errors with a visual-only summary or move focus on every blur
ux_guidelines.good_example:
There is a problem

Enter an email address
ux_guidelines.bad_example: Toast only with no field links or focus target

ux_guidelines.description: Short multi-line headings may use balanced wrapping as a progressive visual heuristic
ux_guidelines.do: Bound the measure and test natural-wrap fallback across widths fonts and locales
ux_guidelines.dont: Promise an exact final line or insert blanket nonbreaking spaces or hardcoded br tags
ux_guidelines.bad_example: Heading copy rewritten with forced last-line breaks

ux_guidelines.description: URLs identifiers and user content must not force horizontal overflow
ux_guidelines.do: Use overflow-wrap anywhere and let flex or grid text children shrink
ux_guidelines.dont: Apply word-break break-all to all prose

ux_guidelines.description: Text must remain available at narrow widths zoom and user spacing overrides
ux_guidelines.do: Use fluid sizes content-driven height and unitless line height
ux_guidelines.dont: Clip text in fixed-width or fixed-height boxes

ux_guidelines.description: Headings actions errors safety text and distinguishing names need complete access
ux_guidelines.do: Wrap stack resize or provide a visible full-detail path
ux_guidelines.dont: Clamp essential meaning only to make cards uniform
ux_guidelines.good_example: Action label wraps or opens full details
ux_guidelines.bad_example: Primary action shown only as an unexplained ellipsis

ux_guidelines.description: Badges communicate state while chips or tags represent values or actions
ux_guidelines.do: Choose static or interactive markup from the label's meaning and ownership
ux_guidelines.dont: Make every pill clickable or encode status with color alone

ux_guidelines.description: Filter chips and editable value collections must preserve labels when space or text size changes
ux_guidelines.do: Wrap the collection or use an operable +n disclosure for hidden overflow values
ux_guidelines.dont: Force all chips into one clipped row or hide overflow values

ux_guidelines.description: A badge chip or pill label should stay whole on one line when practical and disclose unavoidable truncation
ux_guidelines.do: Bound only unpredictable values; use nowrap with a shrinkable label; expose full text to keyboard pointer and touch users
ux_guidelines.dont: Let one compact label wrap to a second line or use a hover-only tooltip
ux_guidelines.good_example: Flexible label with min-width 0 and an operable full-value disclosure
ux_guidelines.bad_example: Fixed-width badge wraps to second line or clips with title-only recovery

ux_guidelines.description: Interactive chips need a native role accessible name state keyboard operation and visible focus
ux_guidelines.do: Prefer a button and expose pressed or selected state that matches the visible label
ux_guidelines.dont: Use a clickable div or reveal the only action on hover

ux_guidelines.description: Async badge and count changes should announce a meaningful contextual status without moving focus
ux_guidelines.do: Use one appropriate atomic status message such as 3 items in cart
ux_guidelines.dont: Announce a bare number or make every badge a competing live region

ux_guidelines.description: Rapid compact-control changes can interrupt an in-flight transition
ux_guidelines.do: Cancel or replace prior motion; set the final semantic state directly and handle cancellation cleanup
ux_guidelines.dont: Depend on animationend or transitionend for required state correctness
ux_guidelines.bad_example: Enable the chip only inside transitionend

motion.Keywords: hover, button, opacity, lift, press feedback
motion.Framework Notes: Bind on mouseenter/mouseleave; in React wrap in a ref + useEffect (or onMouseEnter/onMouseLeave props directly calling gsap.to); Use matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') to skip non-essential motion and render the final state immediately
motion.Do: Keep displacement under 2px so it reads as feedback not motion
motion.Don't: Don't animate layout-affecting props (width/height/margin) on hover
motion.Performance Notes: Runs on transform/opacity only so it stays on the compositor thread

motion.Keywords: hover, card, scale, tilt, cursor feedback
motion.GSAP Snippet: gsap.to(el, { y: -4, scale: 1.02, boxShadow: '0 12px 24px rgba(0,0,0,0.12)', duration: 0.25, ease: 'power2.out' });
motion.Framework Notes: Use gsap.quickTo(el, 'y') for cards with many hover targets to avoid re-creating tweens every event; Use matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') to skip non-essential motion and render the final state immediately
motion.Do: Pair with a matching mouseleave tween that reverses the same properties
motion.Don't: Don't leave the hover state stuck if the pointer leaves fast; always attach the reverse tween
motion.Performance Notes: quickTo() avoids GC churn on lists with 20+ hoverable cards

motion.Keywords: hover, magnetic, cursor follow, 3d tilt, removable event listener cleanup
motion.GSAP Snippet: const onPointerMove = (e) => { const r = el.getBoundingClientRect(); xTo((e.clientX - r.left - r.width / 2) * 0.3); yTo((e.clientY - r.top - r.height / 2) * 0.3); }; el.addEventListener('pointermove', onPointerMove); return () => el.removeEventListener('pointermove', onPointerMove);
motion.Framework Notes: Keep a stable named pointer handler so cleanup removes the same function; in React/Vue return the removeEventListener cleanup; use gsap.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') and render x/y at the final neutral state
motion.Do: Clamp the pull strength (e.g. * 0.3) so the element never fully leaves its hit box
motion.Don't: Don't apply magnetic effect to more than 1-2 focal elements per screen; it becomes noisy
motion.Performance Notes: Use will-change: transform on the target element for smoother compositing

motion.Keywords: scroll, fade in, reveal, on view
motion.GSAP Snippet: gsap.from(el, { opacity: 0, y: 12, duration: 0.35, ease: 'power1.out', scrollTrigger: { trigger: el, start: 'top 90%', toggleActions: 'play none none reverse' } });
motion.Framework Notes: Requires the ScrollTrigger plugin registered once via gsap.registerPlugin(ScrollTrigger); Use matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') to skip non-essential motion and render the final state immediately
motion.Do: Keep the y offset small (8-16px) so it reads as a fade, not a slide
motion.Don't: Don't reveal below-the-fold content needed for SEO/crawlers as invisible-by-default without a no-JS fallback
motion.Performance Notes: toggleActions 'play none none reverse' avoids re-triggering on every scroll direction change

motion.Keywords: scroll, slide up, staggered section, reveal
motion.GSAP Snippet: gsap.from(el.children, { opacity: 0, y: 24, duration: 0.5, stagger: 0.08, ease: 'power2.out', scrollTrigger: { trigger: el, start: 'top 85%' } });
motion.Framework Notes: In React use useGSAP(() => {...}, { scope: containerRef }) from @gsap/react to auto-cleanup on unmount; Use matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') to skip non-essential motion and render the final state immediately
motion.Do: Scope the ScrollTrigger to the section container so it doesn't re-scan the whole page
motion.Don't: Don't stagger more than ~8 children; beyond that the last items feel laggy
motion.Performance Notes: Set scroller/markers: false in production; markers is dev-only

motion.GSAP Snippet: gsap.timeline({ scrollTrigger: { trigger: section, start: 'top top', end: '+=150%', scrub: 1, pin: true } }).from('.headline', { opacity: 0, y: 40 }).to('.bg-layer', { yPercent: -20 }, '<');
motion.Framework Notes: Pinning needs the section to have deterministic height; recalc ScrollTrigger.refresh() after images/fonts load; Use matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') to skip non-essential motion and render the final state immediately
motion.Do: Use scrub: true or a small number (0.5-1.5) instead of instant jumps so it feels tied to the scrollbar
motion.Don't: Don't pin more than 1-2 sections per page; excessive pinning fights native scroll feel and hurts mobile UX
motion.Performance Notes: Pinning forces layout reflow; test on mid-tier mobile devices, not just desktop

motion.Framework Notes: Select items with a stable class/data-attribute (not array index) so re-renders in React don't break targeting; Use matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') to skip non-essential motion and render the final state immediately
motion.Do: Keep per-item stagger delay small (0.02-0.04s) for lists longer than 10 items
motion.Don't: Don't stagger by more than 0.1s per item on long lists; total reveal time becomes sluggish
motion.Performance Notes: For virtualized lists, only animate items currently mounted in the DOM

motion.GSAP Snippet: gsap.from('.grid-item', { opacity: 0, scale: 0.92, y: 16, duration: 0.4, stagger: { each: 0.06, from: 'start', grid: 'auto' }, ease: 'back.out(1.4)' });
motion.Framework Notes: grid: 'auto' lets GSAP infer rows/columns from a CSS grid layout for a natural wave stagger; Use matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') to skip non-essential motion and render the final state immediately
motion.Do: Combine with from: 'center' for a bento-grid layout to draw the eye inward first
motion.Don't: Don't use back.out on dense data tables; the overshoot reads as sloppy on informational UI
motion.Performance Notes: Group DOM writes; avoid interleaving layout reads (getBoundingClientRect) between staggered tweens

motion.Keywords: stagger, wave, text reveal, split text
motion.GSAP Snippet: const split = new SplitText(headline, { type: 'chars' }); gsap.from(split.chars, { opacity: 0, y: 20, rotateX: -40, duration: 0.6, stagger: 0.015, ease: 'expo.out' });
motion.Framework Notes: SplitText is included with GSAP 3.13+; register it before use, review the current GSAP license, and keep a plain-text fade fallback; Use gsap.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') to skip character motion and render the readable final state immediately
motion.Do: Revert SplitText on unmount/cleanup (split.revert()) to restore original text nodes for accessibility tools
motion.Don't: Don't split-animate long paragraphs; reserve for short headlines (under ~8 words)
motion.Performance Notes: Splitting text creates one element per character; keep it to headline-length copy only for DOM size

motion.GSAP Snippet: gsap.to(main, { opacity: 0, duration: 0.2, onComplete: () => { navigate(); gsap.fromTo(main, { opacity: 0 }, { opacity: 1, duration: 0.2 }); } });
motion.Framework Notes: Pair with the router's transition hooks (Next.js App Router transitions, React Router's useNavigate, Vue Router's beforeEach/afterEach); Use matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') to skip non-essential motion and render the final state immediately
motion.Do: Preload the destination route's critical assets before the exit tween finishes
motion.Don't: Don't block navigation on animation; cap exit duration at ~250ms so the app never feels unresponsive
motion.Performance Notes: Exit animation should always resolve faster than entrance (asymmetric timing) so back/forward feels snappy

motion.GSAP Snippet: const tl = gsap.timeline(); tl.to('.transition-overlay', { yPercent: 0, duration: 0.4, ease: 'power2.inOut' }).call(navigate).to('.transition-overlay', { yPercent: -100, duration: 0.4, ease: 'power2.inOut', delay: 0.1 });
motion.Framework Notes: Keep the overlay element mounted at the layout root (outside the page component) so it survives the route swap; Use matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') to skip non-essential motion and render the final state immediately
motion.Do: Show a lightweight loading indicator if the destination route's data fetch outlasts the overlay
motion.Don't: Don't tie the overlay's reveal directly to data-fetch completion without a max-wait timeout; a slow API stalls the whole transition
motion.Performance Notes: Prefer CSS transform (yPercent) over top/left to keep the overlay animation on the compositor thread

motion.GSAP Snippet: const state = Flip.getState('.hero-image'); navigate(); Flip.from(state, { duration: 0.6, ease: 'expo.inOut', absolute: true, zIndex: 100 });
motion.Framework Notes: Requires the GSAP Flip plugin; the 'from' and 'to' route must render the same element with a shared data-flip-id; Use matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') to skip non-essential motion and render the final state immediately
motion.Do: Verify the shared element exists in both DOM states before calling Flip.from to avoid a silent no-op
motion.Don't: Don't use shared-element transitions across more than one element pair per navigation; compounding Flips are hard to time correctly
motion.Performance Notes: Flip recalculates layout (FLIP technique) so test on low-end devices for jank

motion.GSAP Snippet: gsap.to('.bg-layer', { yPercent: 10, ease: 'none', scrollTrigger: { trigger: section, scrub: true } });
motion.Framework Notes: Apply parallax to background/decorative layers only, never to text or interactive controls; Use matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') to skip non-essential motion and render the final state immediately
motion.Do: Keep the yPercent delta small (5-15) so foreground and background never desync distractingly
motion.Don't: Don't parallax body copy; it hurts reading comfort and can trigger motion sickness
motion.Performance Notes: will-change: transform on the parallax layer only; remove it after scroll settles to free GPU memory

motion.GSAP Snippet: gsap.utils.toArray('.parallax-layer').forEach((layer, i) => { gsap.to(layer, { yPercent: (i + 1) * -8, ease: 'none', scrollTrigger: { trigger: layer.parentElement, scrub: 0.5 } }); });
motion.Framework Notes: Layer count beyond 3-4 has diminishing visual return and multiplies scroll-listener cost; Use matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') to skip non-essential motion and render the final state immediately
motion.Do: Vary speed per layer (background slowest, foreground fastest) to sell the depth illusion
motion.Don't: Don't let parallax layers overflow their container; clip with overflow: hidden on the wrapper
motion.Performance Notes: Batch all layers under one ScrollTrigger container where possible instead of one per layer

motion.Keywords: loading, skeleton, shimmer, pulse, stop animation offscreen, visibility pause, reduced motion final state
motion.GSAP Snippet: const tween = gsap.to('.skeleton', { backgroundPosition: '200% 0', duration: 1.4, ease: 'sine.inOut', repeat: -1 }); return () => tween.kill();
motion.Framework Notes: Kill the tween when content mounts or the component unmounts; pause it when its IntersectionObserver reports offscreen or document.visibilityState is hidden; when '(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)' matches kill the tween and set the final static skeleton state
motion.Do: Use a CSS gradient background-position sweep rather than opacity pulsing; reads as 'loading' more clearly
motion.Don't: Don't run more than one shimmer loop per skeleton group; sync them under one timeline so the wave reads as a single unit
motion.Performance Notes: repeat: -1 tweens are cheap but must be explicitly killed on unmount or they leak in SPA route changes

motion.Don't: Don't use elaborate loaders for sub-300ms waits; they flash and feel worse than no indicator
motion.Performance Notes: Pause the timeline (tl.pause()) when the loading tab/view is not visible to save CPU on background tabs

charts.Keywords: trend, time-series, line, growth, timeline, progress, accessible chart, keyboard accessible chart
charts.When to Use: Data has a time axis; user needs to observe rise/fall trends or rate of change over a continuous period
charts.When NOT to Use: Fewer than 4 data points (use stat card); more than 6 series (visual noise); no time dimension exists
charts.Data Volume Threshold: <1000 pts: SVG; ≥1000 pts: Canvas + downsampling; >10000: aggregate to intervals
charts.Color Guidance: Primary: #0080FF. Multiple series: distinct colors + distinct line styles. Fill: 20% opacity
charts.Accessibility Notes: Use solid, dashed, and dotted line styles plus direct series labels; never distinguish series by hue alone.
charts.A11y Fallback: Visible data table plus concise trend summary. Keyboard: focus reveals hover values; +/- buttons zoom; Reset restores the full range.

charts.Keywords: compare, categories, bar, comparison, ranking, accessible chart, keyboard accessible chart
charts.When to Use: Comparing discrete categories by magnitude; ranking or ordering is the core insight; categories ≤ 15
charts.When NOT to Use: Categories > 15 (use table or search); data has time dimension (use line); showing proportions (use waffle/stacked)
charts.Data Volume Threshold: <20 categories: vertical bar; 20–50: horizontal bar; >50: paginated table
charts.Color Guidance: Each bar: distinct color. Grouped: same hue family. Always sort descending by value
charts.Accessibility Notes: Use direct category/value labels and group outlines or patterns; never encode category solely by bar color. Do not rely on color alone.
charts.A11y Fallback: Visible sortable data table plus concise comparison summary. Keyboard: focus reveals hover values; focusable headers with Enter/Space sort and aria-sort reports direction.

charts.Keywords: part-to-whole, pie, donut, percentage, proportion, share, accessible chart, keyboard accessible chart
charts.When to Use: ≤5 categories; one dominant segment vs rest; emphasis on visual proportion over exact values
charts.When NOT to Use: Categories > 5; slice differences < 5% (visually indistinguishable); user needs precise values; accessibility-first context
charts.Data Volume Threshold: Max 6 slices; beyond that switch to stacked bar 100%
charts.Color Guidance: 5–6 max colors. Contrasting palette. Largest slice at 12 o'clock. Always label slices with %
charts.Accessibility Notes: Pie charts do not inherently fail WCAG; unlabeled color-only slices are inaccessible. Use direct labels and patterns, with a non-pie fallback. Do not rely on color alone.
charts.A11y Fallback: Percentage data table and concise part-to-whole summary; offer a stacked bar view. Keyboard: focus reveals slice values; Enter/Space drills in; Back button returns.

charts.Keywords: correlation, distribution, scatter, relationship, pattern, cluster, accessible chart, keyboard accessible chart
charts.When to Use: Exploring relationship between two continuous variables; identifying clusters or outliers in a dataset
charts.When NOT to Use: Variables are categorical (use grouped bar); fewer than 20 points (patterns aren't meaningful); mobile-primary context
charts.Data Volume Threshold: <500 pts: SVG; 500–5000: Canvas at 0.6–0.8 opacity; >5000: hexbin or aggregate first
charts.Color Guidance: Color axis: gradient (blue → red). Bubble size: relative to 3rd variable. Opacity: 0.6–0.8 to show density
charts.Accessibility Notes: Combine marker shapes with direct group labels; color may reinforce but must not be the only distinction.
charts.A11y Fallback: Visible data table plus correlation summary. Keyboard: focus reveals point values; labeled start/end range inputs replace brush dragging.

charts.Keywords: heatmap, heat-map, intensity, density, matrix, calendar, accessible chart, keyboard accessible chart
charts.When to Use: Showing intensity/density across a 2D grid; time-based patterns (e.g., activity by hour × day)
charts.When NOT to Use: Fewer than 20 cells (use bar); user needs to read exact values; colorblind users without pattern fallback
charts.Data Volume Threshold: Up to 10,000 cells efficiently; beyond that aggregate; calendar heatmap: 365 cells max per SVG
charts.Color Guidance: Gradient: Cool (blue) to Hot (red). Divergent scale for ±data. Always include numeric color legend
charts.Accessibility Notes: Print values or symbols in cells and use texture/labels in addition to the color scale. Do not rely on color alone.
charts.A11y Fallback: Grid data table plus intensity summary. Keyboard: focus reveals cell values; +/- buttons zoom; Reset restores the grid.

charts.Keywords: geographic, map, location, region, geo, spatial, choropleth, accessible chart, keyboard accessible chart
charts.When to Use: Data has a regional/location dimension; spatial distribution is the core insight for the user
charts.When NOT to Use: Regions have very different sizes making visual comparison misleading (use bar); mobile-primary context
charts.Data Volume Threshold: <1000 regions: SVG; ≥1000: Canvas/WebGL (Deck.gl); global maps: tile-based rendering
charts.Color Guidance: Single color gradient per region group. Categorized colors for discrete types. Legend with clear scale breaks
charts.Accessibility Notes: Label regions directly and pair fills with boundaries or patterns; location meaning cannot depend on color alone.
charts.A11y Fallback: Sortable region table plus geographic summary. Keyboard: arrow keys or labeled pan buttons move the map; +/- buttons zoom; Enter drills into a focused region; Back returns.

charts.Keywords: funnel, flow, conversion, drop-off, pipeline, stages, accessible chart, keyboard accessible chart
charts.When to Use: Sequential multi-stage process; showing conversion or drop-off rates between defined stages
charts.When NOT to Use: Stages aren't sequential; values don't decrease monotonically (use bar); fewer than 3 stages
charts.Data Volume Threshold: 3–8 stages optimal; beyond 8 stages group minor steps into 'Other'
charts.Color Guidance: Stages: single color gradient (start → end). Show conversion % between each stage. Highlight biggest drop
charts.Accessibility Notes: Keep stage names and values visible and distinguish stages with text and boundaries, not only a gradient. Do not rely on color alone.
charts.A11y Fallback: Linear stage table/list plus conversion summary. Keyboard: focus reveals stage values; Enter/Space drills in; Back returns.

charts.Keywords: performance, target, kpi, gauge, goal, threshold, progress, accessible chart, keyboard accessible chart
charts.When to Use: Single KPI measured against a defined target or threshold; dashboard summary context
charts.When NOT to Use: No target or benchmark exists; comparing multiple KPIs at once (use bullet chart grid)
charts.Data Volume Threshold: Single metric per gauge; for 3+ KPIs use bullet chart grid layout
charts.Color Guidance: Performance: Red → Yellow → Green gradient. Target: marker line. Threshold zones clearly differentiated
charts.Accessibility Notes: Place the number and target text beside the gauge and label threshold zones; red/yellow/green alone is insufficient.
charts.A11y Fallback: Visible KPI/target text and a one-row data table plus status summary. Keyboard: focus reveals the same detail as hover.

charts.Keywords: forecast, prediction, confidence, band, projection, estimate, accessible chart, keyboard accessible chart
charts.When to Use: Historical data + model predictions; communicating uncertainty range to non-technical stakeholders
charts.When NOT to Use: No historical baseline; prediction confidence is too low to be useful; audience is not data-literate
charts.Data Volume Threshold: Keep historical window to 30–90 days for readability; forecast horizon ≤ 30% of visible x-axis range
charts.Color Guidance: Actual: solid line #0080FF. Forecast: dashed #FF9500. Confidence band: 15% opacity fill same hue
charts.Accessibility Notes: Use solid actual and dashed forecast lines, direct labels, and a named confidence range; hue alone is insufficient.
charts.A11y Fallback: Visible forecast table plus uncertainty summary. Keyboard: focus reveals hover values; buttons toggle actual/forecast; +/- buttons zoom; Reset restores range.

charts.Keywords: anomaly, outlier, spike, alert, detection, monitoring, deviation, accessible chart, keyboard accessible chart
charts.When to Use: Monitoring a time-series for outliers; alerting users to unexpected spikes or dips in operational data
charts.When NOT to Use: Anomalies are predefined categories (use bar with highlight); real-time context without a pause control
charts.Data Volume Threshold: Stream at ≤60fps with Canvas; batch: up to 10,000 pts; mark anomalies as a separate data layer
charts.Color Guidance: Normal: #0080FF solid line. Anomaly marker: #FF0000 circle + filled. Alert band: #FFF3CD background zone
charts.Accessibility Notes: Mark anomalies with a distinct shape and text annotation as well as color. Do not rely on color alone.
charts.A11y Fallback: Anomaly event list/table plus narrative alert summary. Keyboard: focus reveals point details; alerts are available in the persistent list without hover.

charts.Keywords: hierarchy, nested, treemap, parent, children, breakdown, drill, accessible chart, keyboard accessible chart
charts.When to Use: Showing size relationships within a hierarchy; overview of proportional structure (e.g., budget breakdown)
charts.When NOT to Use: Hierarchy depth > 3 levels (too complex to read); user needs to compare sibling values precisely
charts.Data Volume Threshold: <200 nodes: SVG; 200–1000: Canvas; >1000: paginate or pre-filter before rendering
charts.Color Guidance: Parent nodes: distinct hues. Children: lighter shades of same hue. White separator borders: 2–3px
charts.Accessibility Notes: Label hierarchy nodes and use borders/patterns as well as hue; make the tree table the primary accessible view. Do not rely on color alone.
charts.A11y Fallback: Collapsible tree table plus hierarchy summary; treemap remains supplementary. Keyboard: focus reveals hover values; Enter/Space drills or expands; Back collapses/returns.

charts.Keywords: flow, process, sankey, distribution, source, target, transfer, accessible chart, keyboard accessible chart
charts.When to Use: Showing how quantities flow between nodes; multi-source multi-target distribution
charts.When NOT to Use: Flow directions form loops (use network graph); fewer than 3 source-target pairs; mobile-primary context
charts.Data Volume Threshold: <50 flows: SVG; ≥50: Canvas; >200 flows: aggregate minor flows into 'Other' node
charts.Color Guidance: Gradient from source to target color. Flow opacity: 0.4–0.6. Node labels always visible
charts.Accessibility Notes: Label source, target, and value; use line style or node symbols in addition to gradient color. Do not rely on color alone.
charts.A11y Fallback: Source-to-target flow table plus flow summary. Keyboard: focus reveals hover values; Enter/Space drills into a node; Back returns.

charts.Keywords: waterfall, cumulative, variance, incremental, bridge, delta, accessible chart, keyboard accessible chart
charts.When to Use: Showing how individual positive/negative components add up to a final total (e.g., P&L, budget variance)
charts.When NOT to Use: Changes are not additive; more than 12 bars (readability breaks); audience expects a simple total
charts.Data Volume Threshold: 4–12 bars optimal; beyond 12 aggregate minor items into a single 'Other' bar
charts.Color Guidance: Increases: #4CAF50. Decreases: #F44336. Start total: #2196F3. End total: #0D47A1. Running total line: dashed
charts.Accessibility Notes: Pair increase/decrease bars with signed values and directional icons, not red/green alone. Do not rely on color alone.
charts.A11y Fallback: Running-total table plus variance summary. Keyboard: focus reveals the same value as hover.

charts.Keywords: radar, spider, multi-variable, attributes, dimensions, comparison, accessible chart, keyboard accessible chart
charts.When to Use: Comparing multiple entities across the same fixed set of attributes (e.g., product feature comparison)
charts.When NOT to Use: Axes > 8 (unreadable); values need precise comparison (use grouped bar); audience unfamiliar with radar charts
charts.Data Volume Threshold: 2–3 datasets maximum per chart; 5–8 axes; beyond 8 axes switch to parallel coordinates
charts.Color Guidance: Single dataset: #0080FF at 20% fill. Multiple: distinct hues with 30% fill. Border: full opacity
charts.Accessibility Notes: Use line styles, point shapes, and direct series labels in addition to color. Do not rely on color alone.
charts.A11y Fallback: Raw data table and grouped-bar alternative plus comparison summary. Keyboard: focus reveals values; buttons toggle series.

charts.Keywords: stock, trading, ohlc, candlestick, finance, price, volume, accessible chart, keyboard accessible chart
charts.When to Use: Financial time-series with Open/High/Low/Close data; trading or investment product context only
charts.When NOT to Use: Non-financial audience; no OHLC data available (use line chart); accessibility-first context
charts.Data Volume Threshold: Real-time: Canvas required. Historical: paginate by time range. Max 500 candles visible at once
charts.Color Guidance: Bullish: #26A69A. Bearish: #EF5350. Volume bars: 40% opacity below. Body fill vs hollow for OHLC style
charts.Accessibility Notes: Use filled versus hollow candles and OHLC text values; bullish/bearish meaning cannot depend on color. Do not rely on color alone.
charts.A11y Fallback: Sortable OHLC table plus daily-change summary. Keyboard: focus reveals candle values; +/- buttons zoom; Reset restores range; live updates do not steal focus.

charts.Keywords: network, graph, nodes, edges, connections, relationships, force, accessible chart, keyboard accessible chart
charts.When to Use: Mapping connections between entities; network topology or social graph exploration context
charts.When NOT to Use: Node count > 500 without clustering pre-applied; user needs precise connection counts; mobile context
charts.Data Volume Threshold: ≤100 nodes: SVG; 101–500: Canvas; >500: must apply clustering/LOD before rendering
charts.Color Guidance: Node types: categorical colors. Edges: #90A4AE at 60% opacity. Highlight path: #F59E0B
charts.Accessibility Notes: Use labeled node types, shapes, and edge styles in addition to color; the adjacency view is the accessible source of truth. Do not rely on color alone.
charts.A11y Fallback: Adjacency list/table and relationship summary; tree view when applicable. Keyboard: focus reveals node details; Enter drills; Move up/down/left/right buttons replace drag.

charts.Keywords: distribution, statistical, spread, median, outlier, quartile, boxplot, accessible chart, keyboard accessible chart
charts.When to Use: Showing spread, median, and outliers of a dataset; comparing distributions across multiple groups
charts.When NOT to Use: Fewer than 20 data points per group (distribution is not meaningful); audience unfamiliar with statistical charts
charts.Data Volume Threshold: Any sample size; aggregated representation so rendering is ⚡ Excellent at any volume
charts.Color Guidance: Box fill: #BBDEFB. Border: #1976D2. Median line: #D32F2F bold. Outlier dots: #F44336
charts.Accessibility Notes: Label median, quartiles, whiskers, and outliers directly; do not use color alone for statistical roles.
charts.A11y Fallback: Statistics table plus distribution summary. Keyboard: focus reveals the same statistics as hover.

charts.Keywords: bullet, compact, kpi, dashboard, target, benchmark, range, accessible chart, keyboard accessible chart
charts.When to Use: Dashboard with multiple KPIs side by side; space-constrained contexts where a gauge is too large
charts.When NOT to Use: Single KPI with emphasis (use gauge); data has no defined target range; fewer than 3 KPIs
charts.Data Volume Threshold: Ideal for 3–10 bullet charts in a grid; scales to any count efficiently
charts.Color Guidance: Qualitative ranges: #FFCDD2 / #FFF9C4 / #C8E6C9 (bad/ok/good). Performance bar: #1976D2. Target: black 3px marker
charts.Accessibility Notes: Label every qualitative range and target with text; color is supplementary.
charts.A11y Fallback: Visible KPI/target table plus status summary. Keyboard: focus reveals the same detail as hover.

charts.Keywords: waffle, percentage, proportion, progress, filled, grid, accessible chart, keyboard accessible chart
charts.When to Use: Showing what fraction of a whole is filled; percentage progress in a visually engaging and accessible format
charts.When NOT to Use: More than 5 categories (use stacked bar); exact values matter over visual proportion; very tight space
charts.Data Volume Threshold: 10×10 grid standard (100 cells); for > 5 categories switch to stacked 100% bar
charts.Color Guidance: 3–5 categories max. 2–3px gap between cells. Each category a distinct accessible color pair
charts.Accessibility Notes: Label each category and percentage and add patterns or symbols; filled-cell color alone is insufficient.
charts.A11y Fallback: Percentage table/list plus part-to-whole summary. Keyboard: focus reveals each cell value.

charts.Keywords: sunburst, hierarchy, nested, proportion, radial, circle, accessible chart, keyboard accessible chart
charts.When to Use: Exploring nested proportions where both hierarchy and relative size matter (e.g., org spend breakdown)
charts.When NOT to Use: More than 3 hierarchy levels (outer rings become unreadable); precision matters over overview; mobile
charts.Data Volume Threshold: <100 nodes: SVG; 100–500: Canvas; >500: filter to top N before rendering
charts.Color Guidance: Center to outer: darker to lighter hue. Each level 15–20% lighter. Contrasting border between sectors
charts.Accessibility Notes: Label hierarchy levels and segments and use boundaries/patterns as well as hue; the indented list is primary. Do not rely on color alone.
charts.A11y Fallback: Collapsible indented list/table plus hierarchy summary and breadcrumbs. Keyboard: Enter/Space drills or expands; Back button returns; focus reveals hover detail.

charts.Keywords: root cause, decomposition, tree, hierarchy, drill-down, ai-split, attribution, accessible chart, keyboard accessible chart
charts.When to Use: Decomposing a metric into contributing factors; AI-assisted analysis or BI drill-down scenarios
charts.When NOT to Use: No clear parent-child causal relationship; audience expects a summary rather than exploration
charts.Data Volume Threshold: Up to 5 levels deep; limit visible nodes to 20 per level for readability; lazy-load deeper levels
charts.Color Guidance: Positive impact nodes: #2563EB. Negative impact nodes: #EF4444. Neutral connectors: #94A3B8
charts.Accessibility Notes: Name each node and contribution and use shapes/connector styles in addition to color. Do not rely on color alone.
charts.A11y Fallback: Expandable tree table plus root-cause summary. Keyboard: Enter/Space drills and expands; Back collapses; dedicated expand/collapse buttons expose the same operations.

charts.Keywords: 3d, spatial, immersive, terrain, molecular, volumetric, point-cloud, accessible chart, keyboard accessible chart
charts.When to Use: Scientific/engineering context where Z-axis carries essential info not expressible in 2D
charts.When NOT to Use: 2D projection conveys the same insight; mobile context; accessibility-required environments; standard business dashboards
charts.Data Volume Threshold: WebGL required. Deck.gl: up to 1M points. Three.js: LOD required beyond 50,000 pts
charts.Color Guidance: Depth cues: lighting and shading. Z-axis: color gradient (cool → warm). Transparent overlapping: opacity 0.4
charts.Accessibility Notes: Use labels, shapes, and depth-independent cues; color and 3D position cannot be the only carriers of meaning.
charts.A11y Fallback: Mandatory 2D projection, data table, and spatial summary. Keyboard: rotate/pan buttons and +/- zoom controls replace pointer/VR manipulation; Reset returns the camera.

charts.Keywords: streaming, real-time, ticker, live, velocity, pulse, monitoring, accessible chart, keyboard accessible chart
charts.When to Use: Live monitoring dashboards; IoT/ops data updating at ≥1 Hz; user needs current value at a glance
charts.When NOT to Use: Update frequency < 1/min (use periodic-refresh line chart); flashing content without reduced-motion support
charts.Data Volume Threshold: Canvas/WebGL required. Buffer last 60–300s of data. Downsample older data on scroll
charts.Color Guidance: Current pulse: #00FF00 (dark theme) or #0080FF (light theme). History: fading opacity. Grid: dark background
charts.Accessibility Notes: Show the current value and status text and use line styles or markers in addition to color. Do not rely on color alone.
charts.A11y Fallback: Streaming data table plus current-value/trend summary. Keyboard: Pause/Resume button controls updates; focus reveals values; +/- buttons zoom; Reset restores range.

charts.Keywords: sentiment, emotion, nlp, opinion, feeling, text-analysis, accessible chart, keyboard accessible chart
charts.When to Use: NLP output visualization; exploratory analysis of text corpus sentiment; frequency-weighted keyword overview
charts.When NOT to Use: Precise values matter (word size is inherently imprecise); screen-reader context; corpus < 50 items
charts.Data Volume Threshold: 50–5000 terms optimal. Beyond 5000: apply top-N filtering before render. Avoid on mobile
charts.Color Guidance: Positive: #22C55E. Negative: #EF4444. Neutral: #94A3B8. Word size maps to frequency
charts.Accessibility Notes: Expose every term, count, and sentiment as text; size and color are supplementary only.
charts.A11y Fallback: Sortable term table/list plus sentiment summary; word cloud is supplementary. Keyboard: focus reveals word details; labeled controls filter with Space/Enter.

charts.Keywords: process, mining, variants, path, bottleneck, log, event, accessible chart, keyboard accessible chart
charts.When to Use: Analyzing event logs to visualize actual process flows; identifying bottlenecks and deviations in ops/product funnels
charts.When NOT to Use: No event log data available; audience expects a static flowchart (use diagram tool); node count > 100 without pre-filtering
charts.Data Volume Threshold: <30 nodes: SVG; 30–100: Canvas; >100: apply variant filtering (top 80% of cases) before rendering
charts.Color Guidance: Happy path: #10B981 thick line. Deviations: #F59E0B thin line. Bottleneck nodes: #EF4444 fill
charts.Accessibility Notes: Label nodes and paths and use shapes/line styles in addition to color; bottlenecks require text annotations. Do not rely on color alone.
charts.A11y Fallback: Path summary table plus bottleneck narrative. Keyboard: Move buttons replace drag; focus reveals node details; Enter activates a node; Back returns.

app_interface.Description: Icon-only buttons must expose an accessible label
app_interface.Do: Set accessibilityLabel or label prop on icon buttons
app_interface.Don't: Icon buttons without accessible names

app_interface.Description: All inputs must have a visible label and an accessibility label
app_interface.Do: Pair Text label with input and set accessibilityLabel
app_interface.Don't: Inputs with placeholder only

app_interface.Description: Interactive elements must expose correct roles/traits
app_interface.Do: Use accessibilityRole/button/link/checkbox etc.
app_interface.Don't: Rely on generic views with no roles

app_interface.Description: Async status updates should be announced to screen readers
app_interface.Do: Use accessibilityLiveRegion or announceForAccessibility
app_interface.Don't: Update text silently with no announcement

app_interface.Description: Decorative icons should be hidden from screen readers
app_interface.Do: Mark decorative icons as not accessible
app_interface.Don't: Have screen reader read every icon

app_interface.Keywords: touch target size platform runtime arbitration iOS 44pt Android 48dp web 24 CSS px React Native hitSlop
app_interface.Description: Native targets use 44pt on iOS and 48dp on Android; web WCAG 2.2 has a separate 24 by 24 CSS px minimum with exceptions
app_interface.Do: Select 44pt for iOS and 48dp for Android at runtime; evaluate web targets separately against WCAG 2.5.8 and its exceptions
app_interface.Don't: Collapse iOS 44pt, Android 48dp, and web 24 CSS px into one cross-platform number
app_interface.Code Example Good: Platform.select({ ios: 44, android: 48 }); // web: evaluate 24 CSS px + WCAG exceptions

app_interface.Description: Adjacent touch targets need enough spacing
app_interface.Do: Keep at least 8dp spacing between touchables
app_interface.Don't: Cluster many buttons with no gap

app_interface.Description: Custom gestures must not break system scroll/back
app_interface.Do: Reserve horizontal swipes for carousels
app_interface.Don't: Full-screen custom swipe conflicting with back
app_interface.Code Example Bad: PanResponder on full screen blocking back

app_interface.Description: Back navigation should be predictable and preserve state
app_interface.Do: Use navigation.goBack and keep screen state
app_interface.Don't: Reset stack or exit app unexpectedly

app_interface.Description: Bottom tab bar should have at most 5 primary items
app_interface.Do: Use 3–5 tabs and move extras to More/Settings
app_interface.Don't: Overloaded tab bar with many icons

app_interface.Description: Modals/sheets must have clear close actions
app_interface.Do: Provide close button and swipe-down where platform expects
app_interface.Don't: Trapping users in modal with no obvious exit

app_interface.Description: Returning to a screen should restore its scroll and form state
app_interface.Do: Keep components mounted or persist state
app_interface.Don't: Reset list scroll and form inputs on every visit

app_interface.Description: Show visible feedback during network operations
app_interface.Do: Use ActivityIndicator or skeleton for >300ms operations
app_interface.Don't: Leave button and screen frozen

app_interface.Description: Confirm successful actions with brief feedback
app_interface.Do: Show toast/checkmark or banner
app_interface.Don't: Complete actions silently with no confirmation

app_interface.Description: Show clear error messages near the problem
app_interface.Do: input-level error + summary banner
app_interface.Don't: Only change border color with no explanation

app_interface.Description: Validate inputs on blur or submit with clear messaging
app_interface.Do: Validate onBlur and onSubmit
app_interface.Don't: Validate on every keystroke causing jank

app_interface.Description: Use appropriate keyboardType and returnKeyType
app_interface.Do: Match email/tel/number/search types
app_interface.Don't: Use default keyboard for all inputs

app_interface.Description: Guide users through form fields with Next/Done flows
app_interface.Do: Use onSubmitEditing to focus next input
app_interface.Don't: Force users to tap each field manually

app_interface.Description: Allow toggling password visibility securely
app_interface.Do: Provide Show/Hide icon toggling secureTextEntry
app_interface.Don't: Force users to type blind with no option

app_interface.Description: Use FlatList/SectionList for lists over ~50 items
app_interface.Do: Use keyExtractor and initialNumToRender appropriately
app_interface.Don't: Render hundreds of items with ScrollView

app_interface.Description: Use correctly sized and cached images
app_interface.Do: Use Image component with proper resizeMode and caching
app_interface.Don't: Load full-resolution images everywhere

app_interface.Description: Debounce scroll/search callbacks to avoid jank
app_interface.Do: Wrap handlers with debounce/throttle
app_interface.Don't: Run heavy logic on every event

app_interface.Description: Micro-interactions should be 150–300ms with native-like easing
app_interface.Do: Use ease-out for enter/ease-in for exit
app_interface.Don't: Use long or linear animations for core UI

app_interface.Description: Respect OS reduced-motion accessibility setting
app_interface.Do: Check reduceMotionEnabled and simplify animations
app_interface.Don't: Ignore user motion preferences

app_interface.Description: Reserve infinite animations for loaders and live data
app_interface.Do: Use looping only where necessary
app_interface.Don't: Keep decorative elements looping forever

app_interface.Description: Body text must be readable and support Dynamic Type
app_interface.Do: Use platform fontScale and at least 14–16pt base
app_interface.Don't: Render critical text below 12pt

app_interface.Description: Support system text scaling without breaking layout
app_interface.Do: Set allowFontScaling and test large text
app_interface.Don't: Disable scaling on all text globally

app_interface.Description: Content must not overlap notches/gesture bars
app_interface.Do: Wrap screens in SafeAreaView or apply insets
app_interface.Don't: Place tappable content under system bars

app_interface.Description: Ensure sufficient contrast in both light and dark themes
app_interface.Do: Use semantic tokens and test both themes
app_interface.Don't: Reuse light-theme grays directly in dark mode

app_interface.Description: Don't rely solely on hidden gestures for core actions
app_interface.Do: Provide visible buttons in addition to gestures
app_interface.Don't: Rely on swipe/shake only with no UI affordance
app_interface.Code Example Good: Swipe to delete + visible Delete button
app_interface.Code Example Bad: Only shake device to undo with no UI

app_interface.Keywords: accessible drag interaction drag single pointer alternative keyboard drag alternative reorder resize move buttons React Native native runtime platform router arbitration iOS Android web
app_interface.Description: React Native drag and reorder operations need a non-drag path selected for the active native runtime
app_interface.Do: Provide named Move up/down buttons or a position menu beside drag handles; route iOS and Android behavior through the runtime platform adapter
app_interface.Don't: Make drag, swipe, or a web-only pointer handler the only way to reorder native content

app_interface.Keywords: password manager passkey paste redundant entry
app_interface.Description: Authentication and multi-step flows should reuse prior values
app_interface.Do: Support password managers passkeys paste and prefilled confirmed values
app_interface.Don't: Force users to retype credentials or the same data in one flow

domains_of_product_architecture.Domain 1: Truth: Optimizes for Human. Mitigates Desirability Risk via empirical market behavior.
domains_of_product_architecture.Domain 2: Logic: Optimizes for System. Mitigates Utility Risk via invisible mathematics, routing, and zero dead-ends.
domains_of_product_architecture.Domain 3: Perception: Optimizes for Surface. Mitigates Aesthetic and Trust Risk via sensory interfaces (obsidian/champagne gold).
domains_of_product_architecture.Domain 4: Reality: Optimizes for Machine & Law. Mitigates Feasibility Risk via WCAG 2.1 AA and hardware limits.
domains_of_product_architecture.Domain 5: Outcomes: Optimizes for Business. Mitigates Viability Risk via Business Model Canvas (BMC) alignment.

macro_laws.friction_budget: Core Use Cases achievable in <= 3 system decisions or clicks.
macro_laws.reversibility: Zero logical dead-ends; every destructive action mandates an explicit Undo or escape route.
macro_laws.state_persistence: Interrupted workflows retain inputted state globally in localStorage or URL hash without forcing restarts.
macro_laws.global_ontology: Master Information Architecture Document (IAD) defining navigation hierarchies and entity models.

meso_laws.millers_law: Maximum 7 (+/- 2) distinct groups of information or parallel choices per view.
meso_laws.rule_of_6: Form inputs, visible table columns, card metrics, and action toolbars capped at <= 6 items per container. Multi-step Stepper for workflows > 6 items.
meso_laws.hicks_law: Maximum 1 primary Call-to-Action (CTA) per screen/drawer; secondary actions require progressive disclosure.
meso_laws.gestalt_bounding: Elements triggering related endpoints share spatial proximity and visual bounding containers.
meso_laws.shatter_request_protocol: Formal waiver required to bypass Meso-level density limits for Expert/Enterprise modes upon proving cognitive friction reduction.

micro_laws.spatial_geometry: Strict 8pt grid alignments (mod 8 == 0 or 4px micro-step), spatial padding tokens, z-index scale.
micro_laws.fitts_law: Minimum 44x44px interactive hit area for all buttons and clickable controls.
micro_laws.chromatic_tokens: Semantic colors only; Red (#DC2626 / #EF4444) strictly reserved for Destructive actions.
micro_laws.typographic_scale: Modular typographic scale, character length capped at <= 60 characters per line for reading prose.
micro_laws.kinetic_sla: Animation durations <= 300ms, visual feedback SLA within <= 100ms.

meta_laws.wcag_accessibility: WCAG 2.1 AA compliant optical contrast ratio >= 4.5:1, ARIA tagging, keyboard tabindex sequencing.
meta_laws.latency_budget: Any async endpoint taking > 400ms automatically mandates a visual skeleton loader.
meta_laws.data_privacy: Prohibits pre-checked consent states and pre-filled PII.

GW-DATA-01.name: Anti-Mock & Live Ground Truth Invariant
GW-DATA-01.rule: Mock or dummy demonstration data is strictly prohibited when live external endpoints exist. Dispatches must exercise verified real destinations (e.g. verified-user@example.com) with visible in-app preview modals (#mailbox-modal) and 100-round continuous regression proof.

GW-HEADLESS-01.name: Zero-Focus-Stealing & Off-Screen Automation Invariant
GW-HEADLESS-01.rule: Host desktop GUI automation, window popping, foreground focus grabbing, and host keystroke simulation (e.g. win32 keybd_event) are strictly prohibited on Windows. All UI and messaging automation MUST execute headlessly on a virtual display (DISPLAY=:99 via WSL2 / Xvfb) or via background daemons.

GW-FALLBACK-01.name: Prohibited Silent Downgrade Invariant
GW-FALLBACK-01.rule: Subsystems and adapters must fail fast and surface actionable exceptions when encountering invalid parameters or endpoint failures. Silently catching errors and falling back to deprecated, obsolete, or disruptive host GUI methods is strictly prohibited.

GW-PROOF-01.name: Empirical Verification Proof Invariant
GW-PROOF-01.rule: Completion claims for tasks, messaging dispatches, or UI changes require fresh terminal execution logs or off-screen framebuffer screenshots confirming physical delivery checkmarks (✓✓) in the current turn.

GW-MCP-01.name: MCP Process Lifecycle Resilience Invariant
GW-MCP-01.rule: MCP servers managed by the agent harness must handle process termination gracefully without leaving orphaned OS handles or triggering unrecoverable client cache errors (exit status 0xffffffff).
